name: Jim_ForCoreCommand
prose: Implements the Tcl "for start test next body" command. It returns JIM_ERR with a wrong-args message unless argc is exactly 5. It evaluates the start script with Jim_EvalObj and returns that code unchanged if it is not JIM_OK. It evaluates the test expression (Jim_GetBoolFromExpr); with JIM_OPTIMIZATION and when the test is "var < n" or "var <= n" (n an integer literal or a variable) and the next script is "incr var" on the same variable, it runs a specialised loop that increments the integer variable in place; if any of those shape checks fail, or the variable is not an integer, it falls back to the general loop. The general loop runs while the test is true and the code is JIM_OK or JIM_CONTINUE: it evaluates the body, then the next script, then the test again. After each body evaluation JimCheckLoopRetcode is applied: for JIM_BREAK or JIM_CONTINUE it decrements interp->break_level and, if it is still above 0, the loop ends at once and that code (JIM_BREAK or JIM_CONTINUE) is returned unchanged to the caller. Otherwise on exit, if no such propagation happened and the code is JIM_OK, JIM_CONTINUE or JIM_BREAK, it sets an empty result and returns JIM_OK; any other code (for example JIM_ERR, JIM_RETURN, or an error from the start script, next script or test) is returned unchanged. The reference counts it took on the loop and limit variable names are released before return.
note: jimsh0.c:17507-17684 (argc check 17515-17518, start 17521-17523, optimized loop 17529-17646, general loop 17650-17667, exit 17669-17683); JimCheckLoopRetcode 17460-17468. Reviewer original (omits propagation of JIM_BREAK/JIM_CONTINUE when break_level > 0) right; round15 (break from next with break_level > 0 returns JIM_BREAK, not JIM_OK) right for the body evaluation path (immediate++ at 17619/17654); the next-script path does not call JimCheckLoopRetcode, so a break there ends the loop and returns JIM_OK.

name: Jim_LoopCoreCommand
prose: Implements "loop var ?first? limit ?incr? body". It returns JIM_ERR with a wrong-args message if argc is below 4 or above 6. It evaluates the numeric arguments with Jim_GetWideExpr (a failure of the first or second is returned; the increment's result is ignored, so an invalid increment leaves 1), with the 4-argument form using the first number as the limit and 0 as the start. It sets the variable to the start value and loops while (i < limit and incr > 0) or (i > limit and incr < 0) and the code is JIM_OK: it evaluates the body; JimCheckLoopRetcode on the result returns JIM_BREAK or JIM_CONTINUE immediately when break_level stays above 0 after decrementing; for JIM_OK or JIM_CONTINUE it advances i by incr and stores it into the variable (JIM_ERR returned if the variable cannot be set in the in-place path). On exit, a final code of JIM_OK, JIM_CONTINUE or JIM_BREAK becomes an empty result and JIM_OK; any other code (such as JIM_ERR or JIM_RETURN) is returned unchanged.
note: jimsh0.c:17687-17762 (argc 17695-17698, args 17700-17709, loop 17718-17755, exit 17757-17761). Reviewer original (the wrong-args JIM_ERR path; JIM_BREAK/CONTINUE can be returned despite the prose saying OK) right: the immediate return at 17720-17722 passes the code through when break_level > 0.

name: JimForeachMapHelper
prose: Shared helper for foreach (doMap = 0) and lmap (doMap = 1). It returns JIM_ERR with a wrong-args message unless argc >= 4 and argc is even. It initialises a list iterator for each of the varList and list arguments (heap-allocating the iterator array when there are more than two); if any varList is empty it sets the result "foreach varlist is empty" and returns JIM_ERR. For lmap it creates a result list, otherwise it uses the empty object. Each pass first checks whether all value lists are finished and stops if so; it then assigns the next values to the variables of each pair (missing values become the empty string, a failure of Jim_SetVariable ends the function with that code) and evaluates the script. JimCheckLoopRetcode on the result can end the function with that code when break_level stays above 0. JIM_OK appends the script's result to the lmap list; JIM_CONTINUE continues; JIM_BREAK leaves the loop as success; any other code (JIM_ERR, JIM_RETURN and so on) ends the function and is returned as it is. On normal completion or a break it sets the interpreter result to the result list (empty for foreach) and returns JIM_OK; on the error paths the result list is not set as the result. The iterator array is freed when it was allocated.
note: jimsh0.c:17789-17891 (arg check 17798-17801, varlist empty 17811-17820, loop 17830-17880, out 17881-17883, free 17887-17890). Reviewer original (script error yields JIM_ERR but code propagates the script's retcode such as JIM_RETURN) right: default case at 17877-17878.

name: Jim_ForeachCoreCommand
prose: Calls JimForeachMapHelper(interp, argc, argv, 0) and returns its result; it implements foreach and adds nothing of its own. Result codes and the interpreter result are those of the helper: JIM_ERR for wrong arguments or an empty variable list, the loop body's code when that is not OK, continue or break, and JIM_OK with an empty result otherwise.
note: jimsh0.c:17894-17897. Reviewer round1 (formal contract omits the JIM_ERR and JIM_OK paths) right; contract not given.

name: Jim_LmapCoreCommand
prose: Calls JimForeachMapHelper(interp, argc, argv, 1) and returns its result; it implements lmap. On success (end of lists or a break) the helper sets the interpreter result to the list of results of the iterations whose body returned JIM_OK (iterations ended by continue contribute nothing) and returns JIM_OK; JIM_ERR for wrong arguments or an empty variable list; any other non-OK, non-continue, non-break code from the body is returned unchanged.
note: jimsh0.c:17900-17903, helper 17789-17891. Reviewer round1 (formal contract omits JIM_ERR and JIM_OK/list-result paths) right; contract not given.

name: Jim_UplevelCoreCommand
prose: Implements "uplevel ?level? command ?arg ...?". With argc < 2 it returns JIM_ERR with a wrong-args message. Otherwise, if the first argument starts with a digit or '#' it takes the call frame for that level (Jim_GetCallFrameByLevel) and drops the argument, else it uses the default (one level up); a NULL frame returns JIM_ERR. If after dropping the level fewer than two arguments remain, it returns JIM_ERR with the wrong-args message. It makes the target frame current, evaluates the single script (argc == 2) or the concatenation of the remaining arguments with Jim_EvalObj, restores the original frame pointer and returns the evaluation's code unchanged.
note: jimsh0.c:18723-18765 (argc check 18725, level 18734-18745, remaining-args check 18746-18749, eval 18751-18759, outer else 18761-18763). Reviewer original (wrong-args JIM_ERR when the level consumes the only argument) right; round15 (code explicitly handles argc < 2 with JIM_ERR) right.

name: Jim_DictCoreCommand
prose: Implements the "dict" command; it dispatches on the subcommand in argv[1] (argv[0] is the command name), with the subcommand table and argument-count limits declared with JIM_DEF_SUBCMD (create, get, getdef, getwithdefault, set, unset, exists, keys, size, info, merge, with, append, lappend, incr, remove, values, for, replace, update). A bad subcommand or a wrong argument count returns JIM_ERR through the subcommand parser. Partly read: I read the dispatch skeleton and the return statements, not the individual subcommand implementations. From it: get, getdef/getwithdefault and exists, unset, size and keys/values return JIM_ERR when the underlying dict operation fails and JIM_OK otherwise (keys/values return the result of Jim_DictMatchTypes); merge with argc == 2 (no dictionaries) returns JIM_OK without setting a result (so the interpreter result is whatever it already was); create returns JIM_OK; update with fewer than six arguments or an odd argument count is redirected to the usage handling.

Reviewer round15 (argv[0] is the command name, subcommand is argv[1]) right; round17 (merge with argc == 2 returns JIM_OK without setting the result) right (20300-20301).

name: JimWaitPid
prose: JimWaitPid(pid, status, nohang) is the Windows (MinGW) variant at jimsh0.c:23735-23748: if pid > 0 it opens a process handle h with OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | SYNCHRONIZE) and, if that succeeds, calls waitpid(h, status, nohang) (a local variable named pid shadows the parameter), then CloseHandle(h) unconditionally; if that waitpid result is greater than 0 it returns h (a handle value that has already been closed by the CloseHandle just before), otherwise it returns JIM_BAD_PHANDLE. It returns JIM_BAD_PHANDLE also when pid <= 0 or OpenProcess fails. *status is only written by waitpid. A separate POSIX definition elsewhere is a macro for waitpid (jimsh0.c:1242).
note: jimsh0.c:23735-23748 (open 23738, waitpid 23740, CloseHandle 23741, return h 23743, bad handle 23747). Reviewer round2 (omits a GetProcessId failure path) is about code not present in this version; round15 (double-close claim false when waitpid returns -1) right here: CloseHandle runs once per OpenProcess handle in this function and the function itself does not return a freshly closed handle when waitpid returns <= 0.

name: JimCreatePipeline
prose: JimCreatePipeline(interp, argc, argv, pidArrayPtr, inPipePtr, outPipePtr, errFilePtr) (jimsh0.c:5690-6142) starts the processes of an exec pipeline and returns the number of processes, or -1 on error with the interpreter result set. Partly read: I read the redirection setup and the per-process loop by returns, gotos and descriptor handling, not the argument parsing from 5690 to 5780. It parses redirection words (<, <<, <@, >, >>, >@, 2>, 2>@, >&, |&) into input, output and error targets; bad arguments return -1 through badargs. It sets up the input descriptor (a temporary file for here-strings, a file, a channel descriptor, or a pipe when the caller wants one through inPipePtr), the final output descriptor (file, channel, or a pipe through outPipePtr) and the error descriptor (a file, channel, the output descriptor, or a temporary file reported through errFilePtr), each failure going to the error label. For each command stage it creates a pipe when it is not the last stage, starts the process (JimStartWinProcess on MinGW, or vfork/fork, with the child redirecting stdin/stdout/stderr with dup2 and closing the other descriptors), stores the handle in the pid array and closes the parent's copies of the stage's input and output descriptors. A fork or start failure goes to the error label. On success it closes the remaining inputId, lastOutputId and errorId descriptors, restores the environment and returns numPids. The error label closes the caller-visible descriptors (*inPipePtr, *outPipePtr, *errFilePtr), the pipe pair still held in pipeIds, detaches the started pids and frees the pid array, sets numPids to -1 and goes through the common cleanup. It does not close outputId (the current stage's output descriptor) at the error label; in the last stage lastOutputId has been moved into outputId (5979-5980), so a failure to start the last stage leaves that descriptor open.
note: jimsh0.c:5690-6142 (input 5856-5890, output 5895-5916, error 5919-5952, stage loop 5957-6091, success cleanup 6097-6110, error label 6113-6141). Reviewer round15 (on final-stage fork failure, lastOutputId/outputId is not closed, so not all pipe fds are closed) right (5979-5980 clears lastOutputId and the error label never closes outputId). Packet name 'exec-pipeline' was a placeholder.

name: JimParseVar
prose: JimParseVar(pc) parses the text after a '$' for the Jim tokenizer and returns JIM_OK or JIM_ERR. It advances past the '$'. With EXPRSUGAR_BRACKET defined and '[' next it parses a command and sets the token type to JIM_TT_EXPRSUGAR, returning JIM_OK. Otherwise it records tstart and the token type JIM_TT_VAR; for ${name} it scans to the closing '}' (counting newlines), sets tend to the last character before it, and skips the '}' if present. Otherwise it scans a name of alphanumerics, '_', bytes >= 0x80 and '::' runs; if '(' follows it scans to the matching ')' (handling backslashes), sets the token type to JIM_TT_DICTSUGAR, and if no match is found and some ')' was seen it rewinds to just after the last ')'; when EXPRSUGAR_BRACKET is not defined a name starting with '(' becomes JIM_TT_EXPRSUGAR. It sets tend to the last character consumed. Finally, if no characters were consumed (tstart equals the current position) it backs up one character and returns JIM_ERR, otherwise JIM_OK; the braced form ${} consumes the braces, so it returns JIM_OK with an empty name (tend before tstart), not JIM_ERR.
note: jimsh0.c:8238-8337 (bracket 8244-8250, braced 8257-8273, name 8274-8291, dict sugar 8292-8328, ifndef 8323-8327, result 8331-8336). Reviewer round1 (EXPRSUGAR for $( ) under #ifndef EXPRSUGAR_BRACKET) right; round2 and round15 (${} returns JIM_OK, not JIM_ERR) right.

name: idxPopulateStat1
prose: Static function idxPopulateStat1(p, pzErr) in the sqlite3expert code of shell.c (14556-14654); the packet's placeholder name was an unnamed excerpt. Returns an SQLite result code. If p->iSample is 0 it returns SQLITE_OK without doing anything. It finds the largest index (idxLargestIndex): if that fails or nMax <= 0 it returns that code. It then runs "ANALYZE; PRAGMA writable_schema=1" on p->dbm, allocates an IdxRemCtx sized for nMax slots, registers two SQL functions (sqlite_expert_rem on p->db when iSample is 100 or on p->dbv otherwise, and sqlite_expert_sample on p->db), prepares three statements and loops over all indexes of tables: for each (skipping rows with NULL names), when iSample < 100 and the table changed it builds the sample table (a failure ends the loop), then calls idxPopulateOneStat1. After the loop, if rc is OK and iSample < 100 it runs "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp.<unique table>" on p->dbv and stores its result in rc (so a failure of that DROP is returned). It finalizes the three statements (merging their errors into rc), frees the context slots and context, and if rc is OK runs "ANALYZE sqlite_schema" on p->dbm. On the paths that get past the three early returns it removes the two registered functions from p->db and drops the temporary table on p->db at the end, ignoring those results, and returns rc. Any error code from an earlier step is returned instead of continuing, except that the cleanup after the loop runs in every case that got past the allocation.
note: shell.c:14556-14654 (early returns 14577-14580, exec 14582, functions 14589-14599, prepares 14601-14610, loop 14612-14627, DROP with rc 14628-14632, finalize 14634-14636, free 14638-14643, ANALYZE 14645-14647, cleanup 14649-14652, return 14653). Reviewer round15 (return list omits the error from DROP TABLE IF EXISTS temp on p->dbv) right (14629-14631 assign rc).

name: sqlite3_intck_step
prose: sqlite3_intck_step(p) advances an incremental integrity check by one step and returns p->rc. If p->rc is not SQLITE_OK at entry it does nothing and returns that code. Otherwise it frees any previous message and sets zMessage to NULL. If bCorruptSchema is set it sets rc to SQLITE_DONE (without checking any further objects). Else if there is no active check statement it calls intckFindObject: if rc is still OK and there is an object it builds and prepares the check SQL (rc may become an error from preparing) and frees the saved key, and if there is no object left it sets rc to SQLITE_DONE; if intckFindObject returned SQLITE_CORRUPT it converts rc to SQLITE_OK, sets zMessage to "corruption found while reading database schema" and sets bCorruptSchema so that the next step returns SQLITE_DONE. If a check statement exists it steps it: a row is the normal case and changes nothing; otherwise it finalizes the statement, clears it, resets nKeyVal, and if the finalize result is SQLITE_CORRUPT it sets rc back to SQLITE_OK and records "corruption found while scanning database object %s" in zMessage. It returns p->rc, so after this call the result can be SQLITE_OK (more to do or a message to read), SQLITE_DONE (nothing more to check, reached when all objects are finished or the schema was found corrupt) or another error code; corruption is reported through the message with rc OK, and zMessage is freed only at the start of the next step (it stays set after an error return).
note: shell.c:15998-16050 (entry 15999, message free 16001-16004, corrupt schema 16006-16007, find object 16009-16028, step 16031-16046, return 16049). Reviewer original (corruption sets rc OK with zMessage; message not cleared when rc is not OK) right; round15 (bCorruptSchema returns SQLITE_DONE before all objects are checked) right (16006-16007).

name: shell_callback
prose: shell_callback(pArg, nArg, azArg, azCol, aiType) is the sqlite3_exec row callback of the shell and always returns 0 (lines 22887 and 23301); the packet name was outside the slice but the function starts at shell.c:22877. If azArg is NULL it returns 0 at once, writing nothing and leaving p->cnt unchanged (this is the first statement of the function). Otherwise it switches on p->cMode and writes to p->out: MODE_Count and MODE_Off write nothing; MODE_Line prints each column as name = value with a row separator between rows (p->cnt++ > 0); MODE_Explain and MODE_ScanExp print a header on the first row (p->cnt++ == 0) and then the row; MODE_Semi and MODE_Pretty print schema text (pretty-printed with indentation for MODE_Pretty); MODE_List, MODE_Www/MODE_Html, MODE_Tcl, MODE_Csv, MODE_Quote and MODE_Ascii print an optional header on the first row (when p->showHeader, or always for MODE_Www) and then the row in their format, with p->cnt incremented in each; MODE_Insert prints an INSERT statement; MODE_Json prints a JSON object per row; MODE_EQP calls eqp_append with atoi of azArg[0] and azArg[1] and azArg[3]. The azArg == NULL checks inside several cases are therefore never true when execution reaches them, because of the early return. Partly read: I read the structure and the per-mode counter handling, not each mode's formatting code. Modes handled in separate columnar code (column, box, table, markdown) have no case in this switch.
note: shell.c:22877-23302 (early return 22887, switch 22888-23300, return 23301). Reviewer round15 (azArg == NULL does not return at once; List/Www/Tcl/Csv write headers and Csv dereferences azArg) wrong: the early return at 22887 precedes every mode.

name: do_meta_command
prose: do_meta_command(zLine, p) executes one dot-command and returns an int; the function spans shell.c:28804-32444 and the packet slice (31746-32016) is a fragment of it. Partly read: I read the head, the tail, and the slice's .testcase and .testctrl parts, not the other ~3000 lines of command bodies. At entry, if an expert session is open it finishes it. It tokenizes zLine in place from index 1 into at most 51 arguments (single or double quotes group a token; backslashes are resolved in double-quoted tokens) and terminates the list with NULL; with no tokens it returns 0. It clears the temp file and then runs one if/else chain keyed on the first letters of the command name (names may be abbreviated). Unknown commands print "unknown command or invalid arguments" and set rc to 1. Most command errors set rc = 1 and go to meta_command_exit, which decrements p->outCount (resetting output when it reaches 0), resets p->bSafeMode to p->bSafeModePersist and returns rc; commands that end the process or need an immediate exit use other paths. In the part read: .testcase redirects output to testcase-out.txt; if that file cannot be opened it prints "cannot open 'testcase-out.txt'" and the command still ends with rc 0 (no rc = 1 in that branch); .testctrl parses its option and may set rc = 1 on usage errors (goto meta_command_exit at 31871, 31888, 31979), and for the cases that call sqlite3_test_control it records rc2 and isOk (isOk 1, 2 or 3 selects how the result is printed, with 3 meaning no output, not an error code). The return value is therefore 0 on success, 1 on usage or command errors, and the per-command values I did not read.
note: shell.c:28804-32444 (head 28804-28846, .testcase 31799-31804, .testctrl 31849-32150, unknown command 32431-32434, exit 32437-32443). Reviewer round15 (.testcase open failure prints an error but leaves rc 0) right (31804); round17 (omits return value 3 from .testctrl optimizations, rc2 = isOk = 3) right as an internal printing mode at 32013, not a returned code; my claim of the overall return values is limited to 0 and 1 because I did not read the rest.

name: do_meta_command
prose: Same function as the previous entry (do_meta_command(zLine, p), shell.c:28804-32444); this slice (32017-32274) is a fragment of its .testctrl dispatch and following commands. The function tokenizes the dot-command line in place, returns 0 for an empty line, runs the matching command and exits through meta_command_exit, which decrements outCount (resetting output at 0), restores bSafeMode from bSafeModePersist and returns rc. Unknown commands print an error and give rc 1; usage and execution errors normally set rc = 1; some helper-based commands return the helper's code and some commands exit the process. In the .testctrl part, each handled control calls sqlite3_test_control with the arguments of its case and sets isOk to say how the value is printed (1 for a plain number, 3 for nothing printed, as seen at 32013-32150); an unrecognised or bad usage prints help and sets rc = 1. Partly read: the .import and other command bodies in this fragment were not read, so I do not state what a .import with no columns returns.
note: shell.c:28804-32444 (testctrl 31849-32150, unknown command 32431-32434, exit 32437-32443). Reviewer round17 (.import with no columns returns 1, not 0) not checked: the .import body is not in the parts I read.

name: doAutoDetectRestore
prose: doAutoDetectRestore(p, zSql) implements the shell's state machine that detects a database dump being restored; it returns an SQLite result code (SQLITE_OK unless a statement fails). Nothing happens when p->eRestoreState >= 7. State 0: if safe mode is off and zSql starts with "PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF;" it moves to state 1, otherwise to 7. State 1: if zSql starts with "BEGIN TRANSACTION;" it prepares and steps "SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_schema LIMIT 1" on p->db (rc may be set by the prepare/finalize); the input is treated as a dump only if the database is empty and rc is OK; for a dump it reads the DEFENSIVE and DQS_DDL settings, turns defensive off and DQS_DDL on, and sets eRestoreState to (defensive ? 2 : 0) + (dqs ddl ? 4 : 0), so the value can be 0, 2, 4 or 6; otherwise (not a dump or rc not OK) it sets state 7. Any state from 2 to 6 uses the default branch: once sqlite3_get_autocommit says no transaction is open, it restores defensive mode if bit 2 is set and turns DQS_DDL off if bit 4 is set, and sets state 7; while a transaction is still open it changes nothing. A state value of 0 produced by state 1 (both settings were off) is handled by the state 0 case on the next call, not by the default branch.
note: shell.c:32602-32667 (state 0 32607-32619, state 1 32621-32649, default 32651-32662). Reviewer original (eRestoreState can be 0 after state 1, not only 2-6) right: 32644 yields 0 when both settings were off, and then the next call runs the state 0 branch again, not the default branch, and that value is then handled by case 0 on the next call.

name: re_match
prose: re_match(pRe, zIn, nIn) runs the compiled regular expression pRe over the nIn-byte UTF-8 input and returns 1 if some match is accepted, 0 if not, and -1 if allocating the state sets fails (sqlite3_malloc64 returning NULL); the function starts at shell.c:7274. If the regex has a literal prefix (nInit > 0) it skips forward to the first position where that prefix occurs and returns 0 if none exists; the matching then starts at that first occurrence only, so a later occurrence of the prefix is not tried separately by this skip loop (the pattern's own states may still match later). It uses stack space for the state sets when pRe->nState is small, otherwise heap memory freed before returning. It then steps a nondeterministic automaton character by character while characters remain and the next state set is non-empty, handling the operations MATCH, ATSTART, ANY, WORD, NOTWORD, DIGIT, NOTDIGIT, SPACE, NOTSPACE, BOUNDARY, ANYSTAR, FORK, GOTO, ACCEPT, and character classes (CC_INC and CC_EXC with values and ranges); ACCEPT ends the scan with success. After the loop, if the remaining state set contains an ACCEPT (after following GOTOs) it returns 1; otherwise 0.
note: shell.c:7274-7420 (prefix 7290-7298, allocation 7302-7307, loop 7314-7411, final accept check 7412-7419). Reviewer round15 (only the first zInit occurrence is tried; some prefix overclaims) right (7292-7298).

name: lookupName
prose: Static function lookupName (sqlite3.c:108312-108888) resolves a column reference expression against the name contexts and returns a Walker code. It searches the FROM tables (and joins with USING/NATURAL columns, rowid aliases, trigger new/old rows, the RETURNING and alias lists, and outer name contexts) counting matches in cnt. Partly read: I read the counting logic and the exits, not each lookup branch. If cnt is not exactly 1 at the end it deletes the partial full-join match list when relevant and reports an error with sqlite3ErrorMsg: "no such column" when cnt is 0 or "ambiguous column name" when more than one match, with the db/table/column qualifiers or, for a double-quoted name that matched nothing, a message suggesting a string literal, and records the error offset; in this case the function ends through the common exit and returns WRC_Abort (the error is set here, not left for the caller). A misused aliased aggregate, aliased window function or row value also sets an error message and returns WRC_Abort at once. If exactly one match is found it converts the expression in place (it frees pLeft and pRight of the expression and turns it into a TK_COLUMN or related node), updates the matching table's colUsed bits, calls the authorizer read hook if configured, propagates usage counts through the enclosing name contexts, and returns WRC_Prune. The special handling of a bare name that matches no column (the block at 108750-108779, which includes a TK_NULL conversion for some rowid cases) was not read, so I make no claim on it.
note: sqlite3.c:108312-108888 (cnt counting 108407-108531, cntTab 108654-108661, aliased errors 108706-108717, error reporting 108792-108827, free left/right 108835-108838, colUsed 108857-108860, exit 108866-108886: WRC_Prune when cnt == 1, else WRC_Abort). name: resolveExprStep
prose: Static Walker callback resolveExprStep(pWalker, pExpr) at sqlite3.c:108987-109486 (the packet name sqlite3ResolveExprStep does not exist) that resolves names and checks one expression node during sqlite3ResolveExprNames. It switches on pExpr->op: TK_ROW (rowid of the first FROM table), TK_ISNULL/TK_NOTNULL (some paths return WRC_Prune), TK_ID and TK_DOT (call lookupName and return its WRC_Prune/WRC_Abort result), TK_FUNCTION (function lookup and checks; one path returns WRC_Prune at 109204), TK_SELECT/TK_EXISTS/TK_IN (resolve the subselect names), TK_VARIABLE (resolve parameter numbers), TK_IS/TK_ISNOT/TK_BETWEEN and the comparison operators (check that row values are used consistently, error "row value misused"), among others. For other operators nothing special happens. After the switch it returns WRC_Abort if pParse->nErr is non-zero, otherwise WRC_Continue; some cases return WRC_Prune earlier (109062-109092, 109204) and the lookupName result is returned directly. Partly read: I read the switch skeleton and the exits, not the TK_FUNCTION, TK_IN and comparison bodies in detail.

name: sqlite3CodeSubselect
prose: sqlite3CodeSubselect(pParse, pExpr) (sqlite3.c:114085-114203) generates code for a scalar subquery (TK_SELECT) or EXISTS (TK_EXISTS) and returns the register holding the result, or 0 on failure. It returns 0 at once if pParse->nErr is already non-zero (no error flag is set by this function in that case). If the expression already has EP_Subrtn set it reuses the existing subroutine (returns pExpr->iTable, or its result register, without emitting new code for the select). Otherwise, only when the expression does not have EP_VarSelect (that is, it is not correlated with outer queries; variables or triggers can also cause code to run each time in other ways), it emits OP_Once so the subroutine body runs once; it sets up the destination (SRT_Mem for a scalar select, SRT_Exists for EXISTS) builds integer LIMIT expressions (114168 and 114178), runs sqlite3Select on the sub-select and, if that returns non-zero, sets the failure and returns 0 (line 114185); otherwise it patches the OP_Once jump, records the subroutine's start address and register range and returns the result register.

Reviewer original (returns 0 on a pre-existing nErr without setting TK_ERROR) right; round15 (OP_Once only when !EP_VarSelect, not merely non-correlated) right. Partly read: 114117-114132 and 114186-114201 were not read line by line.

name: sqlite3CreateIndex
prose: sqlite3CreateIndex(pParse, pName1, pName2, pTblName, pList, onError, pStart, pPIWhere, sortOrder, ifNotExist, idxType) (sqlite3.c:126926-127516) creates an index or the implied index of a constraint; it returns nothing. It leaves early through exit_create_index (not creating anything) when the parse already has errors or malloc failed, the database cannot be found or the table cannot be located, the table is a system table, a view or a virtual table (error messages "table %s may not be indexed", "views may not be indexed", "virtual tables may not be indexed"), the name clashes (error "there is already a table named %s" or "index %s already exists", the latter silent with IF NOT EXISTS), the authorizer denies the operation, the column list cannot be built, an expression index appears in a PRIMARY KEY/UNIQUE constraint ("expressions prohibited in PRIMARY KEY and UNIQUE constraints"), the key columns cannot be built, or during schema loading the root page is invalid ("invalid rootpage"). On the success path it builds the Index object, links it into the table's index list (immediately when db->init.busy or for an implied index; during a rename it records it in pParse->pNewIndex instead) and, for a CREATE INDEX statement outside schema loading, emits VDBE code to create and fill it; ownership of pIndex passes to the table or pParse. At exit_create_index it frees pIndex if it was not handed over (this also frees it on any early error), reorders the table's index list so REPLACE-conflict indexes come first, and frees pPIWhere, pList, pTblName and the name string. Out-of-memory is recorded in db->mallocFailed rather than in pParse. Partly read: I read the early exits and the tail, not the key-column construction in the middle (127126-127400).
note: sqlite3.c:126926-127516 (exit gotos at 126958-127382, init.busy link 127469-127473, rename 127474-127478, exit_create_index 127481-127515). Reviewer round15 (malloc failure is recorded in db->mallocFailed, not pParse; the rename path links pIndex rather than freeing it) right (127474-127478 sets pParse->pNewIndex and clears pIndex).

name: sqlite3CreateIndex
prose: Same function as the previous entry (sqlite3CreateIndex, sqlite3.c:126926-127516); this slice (127367-127628) covers its tail and the start of the next function (sqlite3DropIndex), so the head was cut. In the part of sqlite3CreateIndex covered it checks a "invalid rootpage" during schema loading, gets a Vdbe (returning through exit_create_index if none), emits the index creation and population code unless it is being loaded from the schema, links the new Index into the table's list (immediately when db->init.busy or for an implied index; during a rename it stores it in pParse->pNewIndex), and at exit_create_index frees any unlinked pIndex, moves REPLACE-conflict indexes to the front of the table's list, and frees pPIWhere, pList, pTblName and zName. The rest of the slice belongs to sqlite3DropIndex and is not described here.

name: sqlite3CodeVerifySchemaAtToplevel
prose: Static function sqlite3CodeVerifySchemaAtToplevel(pToplevel, iDb) (sqlite3.c:128336-128347) records that the schema cookie of database iDb must be verified by the statement being compiled. If the bit for iDb is not yet set in pToplevel->cookieMask it sets it and, when temp databases are enabled and iDb == 1, calls sqlite3OpenTempDatabase(pToplevel) (which may fail and record an error in the parse); if the bit was already set it does nothing. It returns nothing and emits no VDBE code itself. The debug asserts require iDb to be in range and the database to have a Btree or be the temp database (iDb == 1).

Reviewer original (temp DB opened only when the cookie bit was clear; precondition omits pBt != 0 or iDb == 1) right; round15 (page-size failure sets rc via OOM and leaves no message) concerns sqlite3OpenTempDatabase, which I did not read.

name: sqlite3BeginWriteOperation
prose: sqlite3BeginWriteOperation(pParse, setStatement, iDb) (sqlite3.c:128381-128386) prepares for a statement that may write database iDb. It finds the top-level parse, calls sqlite3CodeVerifySchemaAtToplevel(pToplevel, iDb) (which sets the iDb bit in cookieMask and may open the temp database when iDb == 1 and the bit was clear), sets the iDb bit in pToplevel->writeMask, and ORs setStatement into pToplevel->isMultiWrite (an existing non-zero value stays; the new value is not simply 1 for any non-zero argument, it is the bitwise OR with the argument). It returns nothing and emits no VDBE code itself.
note: sqlite3.c:128381-128386. Reviewer original (omits the cookieMask bit set and possible temp DB open via CodeVerifySchemaAtToplevel) right; round15 (isMultiWrite is ORed with setStatement, not set to 1) right (128385).

name: sqlite3DeleteFrom
prose: sqlite3DeleteFrom(pParse, pTabList, pWhere, pOrderBy, pLimit) (sqlite3.c:129634-130039) generates code for DELETE; it returns nothing. Partly read: I read the control skeleton and exits, not the code generation bodies. It jumps to delete_from_cleanup (freeing the arguments and doing no code generation) if the parse already has errors, the table cannot be found or opened, the view's columns cannot be determined, the table is read-only (system table, triggers, etc.), the authorizer or WHERE name resolution fails, or a WHERE-loop setup (sqlite3WhereBegin) returns NULL or a one-pass step fails. It has separate paths for views (isView, 129757-129774) and virtual tables (IsVirtual, 129965-129984), and runs the WHERE loop through sqlite3WhereBegin with one-pass variants (ONEPASS_SINGLE, ONEPASS_MULTI or off); with eOnePass != ONEPASS_SINGLE it calls sqlite3MultiWrite (129878). When the count-changes memory register is in use (memCnt) it adds the count code and the result column. delete_from_cleanup is the common exit of the error jumps; I did not read what it frees.

name: multiSelectOrderBy
prose: Static function multiSelectOrderBy(pParse, p, pDest) (sqlite3.c:148352-148666; the packet name did not mention the function but it is in the file) implements a compound SELECT (UNION, EXCEPT, INTERSECT) with an ORDER BY by running each side as a co-routine and merging. It returns SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT while rewriting the ORDER BY terms if allocation of a new expression fails, and otherwise returns pParse->nErr != 0 at the end (1 if an error was recorded, else 0). In between it checks and renames the ORDER BY terms to column positions, generates the two co-routine sub-selects, the output subroutine and the merge loop. name: sqlite3SelectPrep
prose: sqlite3SelectPrep(pParse, p, pOuterNC) (sqlite3.c:151385-151399) prepares a SELECT for code generation; it returns nothing. It returns at once if db->mallocFailed is set (without setting any error) or if the select already has SF_HasTypeInfo. Otherwise it calls sqlite3SelectExpand (expand * and subqueries), returns if pParse->nErr is set, calls sqlite3ResolveSelectNames, returns if nErr is set, and then calls sqlite3SelectAddTypeInfo (which, as a macro or function, marks the select SF_HasTypeInfo when it is not compiled out).

name: sqlite3RunVacuum
prose: sqlite3RunVacuum(pzErrMsg, db, iDb, pOut) (sqlite3.c:157275-157540; VACUUM and VACUUM INTO) returns an SQLite result code. It returns SQLITE_ERROR with an error message, before changing anything, if the connection is not in autocommit mode ("cannot VACUUM from within a transaction"), if other statements are active (nVdbeActive > 1), or if pOut is given and is not text; these preconditions apply to both plain VACUUM and VACUUM INTO. Otherwise it saves the connection flags, attaches a temporary database (or the target file for INTO) with execSqlF (a failure goes to end_of_vacuum), begins a transaction, copies the schema and data with execSql statements, copies the temp database over the main file with sqlite3BtreeCopyFile for a plain VACUUM, or commits the INTO copy, and at end_of_vacuum restores the flags, sets db->autoCommit = 1 (this restoration is only reached after the early-return checks), detaches the temporary database and returns rc (the details of these steps were not read). Partly read: I read the early returns, the error gotos and the end-of-function restoration, not the SQL text of each execSql step.

name: exprAnalyze

name: whereOmitNoopJoin
prose: Static function whereOmitNoopJoin(pWInfo, notReady) (sqlite3.c:170833-170904; the packet name sqlite3WhereOmitNoopJoin does not exist) marks the loops of LEFT JOIN tables whose columns are unused as omitted, so no code is generated for them, and returns the updated notReady bitmask. It requires the SQLITE_OmitNoopJoin optimisation to be enabled (asserted) and that the statement is not a DISTINCT aggregate. For each loop from the innermost outwards it considers the loop only when the statement does not want distinct output and the loop does not return a single row (WHERE_ONEROW not set, 170863-170864); it compares the prerequisite masks of terms with pLoop->maskSelf (170871 and 170892) to decide whether anything uses the table; the later part of the loop body (not read in detail) is what omits loops and updates notReady. It returns notReady (170903). Partly read: I read the guards and the return, not the mask arithmetic.
